convoLines.text: "Do you still sing? ...Sorry — weird question. I just realized I haven't heard anyone sing."
"Ha! The creek concerts. I've heard those. Keep going."
"...What's that supposed to mean?" Their voice goes careful.
"Still on whether you still sing."
"Yes. Absolutely. I've been hoping you'd ask." (A little too quickly.)
"Come get air with me. I need to think out loud."
"Here. I made an extra." Lorenzo presses something into your hand — a decent tool, oiled and kept. (Useful. Keep it.)
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"A name. Okay." You say it out loud, trying the shape of it:
🤝 "The Company." It hangs in the air a moment — then Lorenzo grins. It's real now. It has a name, which means it can be lost.
They go very still. Not relaxed-still. Held-still.
"I already told you what happened." Lorenzo crosses their arms. "Asking again doesn't change it."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Can I tell you something? Before the scattering, I said something cruel. I think about it every day."
Victor has an edge today — something curdled.
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Still on what they confided."
"Alright. But I'm not carrying your stuff."
You show them Black Walnut — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. "And I've been walking past it for weeks."
"Don't tell anyone I told you. What's on your mind?"
"Good question." "Have you heard what they're calling Inspiration? Lorenzo is pushing 'The Big Beast'. Everyone's got a name for it and nobody agrees."
"All right. Thank you for telling me."
"I have opinions about the name. I am saving them for when they count."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
🤝 Victor is 👁️ Scout now. Sees trouble first. Warns the party on the road.
"Right. Go on, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Are you angry? At whoever did this. At the sky. At anything."
"Good. Anger's fuel. Just — point it somewhere useful."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Walk with me? I want another pair of eyes on something."
It's quiet at the tree line. Paisley doesn't say much. Sometimes that's the whole point.
"Still on whether you're angry."
"...Fine. This had better be worth it."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
Victor nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
Something crosses their face — quick, then gone. The practiced expression clicks back into place.
"Fine." Sharp. "You want to hear it? I dug it up. I was starving and your hole was right there. Happy now?"
They glance at the fire, then back. The quiet doesn't seem to bother them.
"Sure. I'll be around."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"Can we talk?" Victor shifts their weight. "I need something to do. Anything. Please."
"It's just — What's your first memory? Like, ever. The earliest thing."
"Okay." Something shutters, just slightly.
"Still on your first memory."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want? ...if that makes sense."
"You want to know about that? Okay." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "Jorge always took the burnt piece. Said someone had to. I take it now."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
Paisley nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
"My part? I remember them. Someone has to do it properly."
You show them Wild Ramps — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
A warmth settles over the conversation — they lean in a little.
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"About that question — Have you ever hurt someone? Since all this started."
They nod, slow. "Okay. Thank you for telling me. That couldn't have been easy to say."
"What are you getting at?" A glance away, then back. They're choosing their words now.
"Still on whether you've hurt someone."
A small chill settles between you. They're choosing words more carefully.
"Forget I said anything. What did you want? ...sorry."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
A flicker at the corner of their mouth. Not quite a smile. Not quite anything.
*They've deflected you before. The evidence needs to be heavier this time — one more thread before you speak.*
"Nope. No." Lorenzo shakes their head too fast. "I don't know where you're getting this."
Victor nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
The silence stretches a beat too long. They study their hands.
"Right. Go on, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They nod, already turning away.
"What did you do for fun? Before. The thing you'd do on a perfect Saturday."
"It was. But lifetimes come back around. They do."
"Still on what you did for fun."
"What's the kindest thing someone's done for you out here?"
"I hear you. But don't let the fear eat the good parts. They're real, even when they're rare."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Good question." "Last time things were different. They always are." "They took Abdul — The Secret Deck, on the screens. The whole fire watched. Nobody knew where to look."
"That's the whole of it. Sorry."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Anyway." A small smile.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
Lorenzo nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
"Sure. I'll be around."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"This was good." They mean it.
"About that question — Are you going to stay? With us. For real."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
Whatever warmth was building cools to politeness.
They're rattled — hands busy, eyes everywhere but on you. "I've told you what I've told you."
"Still on whether you're staying."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
Victor nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
Their eyes do the math before their mouth does. You can see the calculation happening.
*They've deflected you before. The evidence needs to be heavier this time — one more thread before you speak.*
"What? No — I mean —" Lorenzo stumbles. "It's... it's complicated. Can we not do this right now?"
You don't answer. The quiet turns pointed.
"Sure. I'll be around."
"Right. Well." That's the whole goodbye.
"You said you were furious. Most days. Still carrying it?"
Paisley has an edge today — something curdled.
They settle in like someone glad you're here.
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
"Sure — Still on that personal stuff."
Something in them almost softens — then doesn't. Not yet.
"Sure — what's on your mind? You'd know about that."
"Good question." "The Secret Deck. They just... took Abdul. Came back like nothing happened. It wasn't nothing."
"Same weather, different day. I keep notes."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
Lorenzo nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"This was good." They mean it.
"This cut — I can't clean it properly one-handed. Will you help me clean it?"
"It's getting worse, not better. If it festers I'm no good to anyone — can't haul, can't hunt, can't watch. Just clean it out and wrap it tight."
They are out on the road, miles from here. Find them when they are back.
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
They glance toward the fire, toward the others — checking who's listening.
*The deflect is a move you know now. It works when what you have is thin. Make it thick.*
"I wasn't a chimney sweep. I was a hunter. There are people from my old life I'd rather never find me. That's all."
"You're a good listener, you know that?" A tired smile.
A neutral quiet returns, the kind where words land normally.
"No, yeah, of course. Forget I asked." They won't forget. They'll just stop asking.
"Still on that wound care."
"Sure. I'll be around."
"No — you're right, it's a lot. Forget it."
"Right. Well." That's the whole goodbye.
"Never mind the pantry run — we got it handled. Thanks anyway. Water's almost gone — 5 liters. Haul the creek with me at dawn? Two buckets each, there and back."
"I checked the cistern three times hoping I misread it. 5 liters. We walk together and each carry two liters back. Creek water still needs boiling."
Your partner is inside the Haven hall. Go through the door to meet them.
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"This one — Jewelweed. Leaf, stem, smell. You won't forget it now."
"I dreamed Lillian was still here. Woke up angry at the dream. Stupid."
"Alright. But I'm not carrying your stuff."
You show them Yarrow — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"I write everything down. It doesn't bring anyone back. It just keeps my hands from shaking."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
Paisley nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"And... scene. Good talk."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
"This was good." They mean it.
Back before, I was nobody special. This is my chance to be someone who matters.
You can feel the history in how they greet you.
The easy manner evaporates. What's left is watching you back.
*You've seen the smooth deflect before — it buys them time, not truth. Thin evidence gets deflected. Bring one more thread before you go again.*
A wall comes down, then — surprisingly — a door opens behind it. "I wasn't a midwife. I was a Mushroom grower. I wasn't protecting myself. I was protecting someone else." Quiet. Real.
"Proving yourself never ends. That's the secret. You just get better at the proving."
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Still on wanting to prove they're useful."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
"...I need to go be quiet for a while."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Do you still count the days? I lost track days ago."
"Okay." Something shutters, just slightly.
"Still on what day it is."
"Someone should watch your back. Might as well be me."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up? Do you understand?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "I dreamed Marcus was still here. Woke up angry at the dream. Stupid."
"I count portions out loud before eating. It doesn't bring anyone back. It just keeps my hands from shaking."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
Stan nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"We're done for now. Not done-done. For now."
They glance at the fire, then back. The quiet doesn't seem to bother them.
"My brain won't shut up. Talking helps. Keep talking."
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
Their eyes do the math before their mouth does. You can see the calculation happening.
*The deflect is a move you know now. It works when what you have is thin. Make it thick.*
"I don't actually want to belong somewhere. I want to leave and find somewhere better. The less of me is out there, the less can be used against me."
"We were just talking. Nothing important."
"I don't know you well enough for that. Ask me again when we've survived something together."
You show them Black Walnut — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"Moving! But — good talk! More later!"
They fill the quiet. "Anyway — where was I?"

d32: Nobody's talking much. The fire feels smaller tonight.
d32: 🕯️ Grayson Boyd is dead — the wild. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d32: What Grayson kept close goes into the ground with them — keepsakes are buried, never taken from the body.
d32: "Grayson's gone." Lorenzo looks at you for a long moment. "You're not Grayson." No heat in it. Just fact. You'll have to earn this face.
d32: The Codex doesn't pause for grief. Lillian blinks — and it's already there, overlaying everything, syncing. No pen. No paper. The mantle just... transfers.
d32: 📖 LEARNED: Herbal Medicine (Level 1). Willow bark = aspirin. Yarrow stops bleeding. Plantain draws out infection. The pharmacy is outside.
d32: 📖 LEARNED: Reading the Land (Level 1). Eat the landscape with your eyes first: green + water + sun means food grows here. Start where those three meet.
d32: 📖 LEARNED: The Forager’s Eye (Level 1). You walk slower and see more. Food was always there; now you notice it.
d32: 📖 LEARNED: Steady Hands (Level 1). Fine work under pressure. Dressing game, stitching wounds, tying snares — no shake.
d32: 📖 LEARNED: Reading Tracks (Level 1). Fresh tracks have sharp edges. Old tracks crumble. You can tell how recently something passed.
d32: 🌟 "MANTLE TRANSFER DETECTED. ...Oh! New face! Same job! Whole new set of tricks. We hardly noticed. (That is a lie. We noticed. The audience CRIED.)"
